## 9. Protective activity when formation changes identity

Denying a reason for B over A does not require preferring A, objecting to B or asserting q's right to exist. The stronger rival can regard both worthwhile lives as genuinely good and B as permissible while denying this comparative favor for an uninvolved responder. Identifying no protected loss therefore answers some objections against B; the positive ground for B remains to explain.

### Separate unknown identity from identity changed by action

Consider an independently proceeding settlement process and a common environmental condition that would cause the specified severe adverse experience in its future inhabitants. An uninvolved participant can correct that condition through independently permitted means. The intervention need not initiate settlement or increase the number of people. The specified worthwhile activities, current people's claims, costs and risks remain assessed.

First, let the process determining who forms be independent of the correction. For each possible formation, the same eventual person would encounter either the corrected or uncorrected environment. Their identity need not be known now. A pairwise same-person account can support this generic protection. No abstract type experiences the benefit; actual people would undergo it in the respective histories. This control establishes neither a lottery among possible selves nor a reason to select another person.

Now compare a configuration in which the same hazard-removing work also alters formative timing. An independently defensible mechanism and identity account must establish that q would arise without intervention and a different r with it. Timing alone is insufficient. The environmental correction and timing change are distinct causal contributions within this history; “incidental” describes their relation to the protective aim, not the identity change's moral irrelevance. These are hypothetical comparisons, not empirical findings about a particular population.

### The affirmative point survives a corrected beneficiary description

Learning that the correction changes identity withdraws the claim that q would personally benefit. It need not withdraw the whole point of the activity: the intervention still changes a condition through which a worthwhile future life would otherwise include the specified adversity. The resulting good is realized in that future life, without returning to the initiator or compensating q with r's experience.

The proposed ground tracks a real contribution. A matched operation with the same timing effect but no hazard reduction lacks this identified protective point. Worsening the hazard would reverse that aspect even if identity consequences remained unchanged. These comparisons examine the operation's effects, not its benevolent name or the responder's motivation. They do not recommend first creating a burden or derive the complete A/B ordering by transitivity through a manufactured repair case.

The defended judgment is that the warranted protective difference remains a consideration for this eligible participant. It is a positive claim about what the action enables within the unfolding, rather than an inference from the absence of an objection. The rival can deny that this particular ground survives identity-changing formation. That disagreement must address the value and practical significance of the protective transformation itself; neither position wins by renaming the beneficiary.

### Preserve a real limiting case

Suppose the chosen method changes an existing family's scheduled access to a resource. In one history, timing is legitimately open to adjustment. In another, an independently warranted undertaking protects the family's specified opportunity until they decide. Identify the actual terms, authority and reliance; calling it a commitment does not establish its validity. The second intervention can frustrate a real existing claim, even though q has no established claim to be created.

That difference may require another method, warrant delay or defeat the proposed action. It does not automatically extinguish every protective consideration. Conversely, removing the undertaking would not create the positive ground; the identified protective contribution supplies the candidate ground. The [commitment and release studies](HUIGEN-SELF-GROUND-AUDIT.md#55-reasons-to-revise-and-powers-to-release) already distinguish a reason for change from authority to make it.

### What the primary comparison changes

The [Kumar–Martin comparison](FUTURE-BEARER-FORMATION-SOURCES.md#future-standpoints-kumar-and-martin) tests whether a generic description preserves the relevant lives and circumstances. We must not attribute an abstract type's counterfactual improvement to a person who could not undergo it. Our proposal instead assesses each history's lived conditions and the action that changes which history develops. The ensuing comparative reason remains to justify; it is not supplied merely by saying “whoever forms.”

This advances a bounded reason for protective activity despite an identity consequence. It leaves creation versus noncreation open, adds no general maximization rule, and establishes no universal permission, duty or particular person's claim against the responder. A genuine loss of constitutive good, protected continuity, authority, causal efficacy or reliability would revise the judgment. The next bridge is the scope of this positive protective ground across eligible participants, with its actual limits retained.

## Future standpoints: Kumar and Martin

Rahul Kumar, “Risking Future Generations”, *Ethical Theory and Moral Practice* 21(2) (2018), 245–257, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10677-018-9880-z). [Link-only provenance, reading scopes and bounded synopsis](../../../../sources/37-ethical-minimum-primary-2026-10-06/future-standpoints/kumar/README.md).

Kumar distinguishes noncomparative grounds for objection from comparison among alternative principles. Generic descriptions support claims of particular people. His account of legitimate expectations and his note 11 exclusion of an existence-interest remain substantive commitments. Root independently read the specified generic-standpoint, entitlement and default-relationship passages; the source investigator read the complete extracted main argument and notes.

D. Valeska Martin, “Navigating Nonidentity: Scanlonian Contractualism and Types of Persons”, *Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy* 29(1) (2024), 86–106, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.26556/jesp.v29i1.3436). [Link-only provenance, root reading scope and bounded synopsis](../../../../sources/37-ethical-minimum-primary-2026-10-06/future-standpoints/martin/README.md).

Martin challenges attributing a type's comparative position to an individual who lacks that position. Her §4 distinguishes unknown identity from identity-changing alternatives and expressly brackets noncomparative objections. It therefore does not by itself refute Kumar's full proposal. Root read the introduction, §§1–3, substantial selected §4 and §5 through a public reproduction; original bytes were not retrieved.

**Our synthesis:** generic description must preserve the relevant differentiated situation. It creates neither another experiencer nor a reason by definition. The scope of a prohibition on imposing risk also does not automatically supply a nonoriginator's reason to intervene. [Section 9](FUTURE-BEARER-FORMATION-ARGUMENT.md#9-protective-activity-when-formation-changes-identity) therefore tests the protective contribution directly and retains current claims. It does not rest on a person's hypothetical opportunity to be either of two different future people, nor require a narrative self as the universal criterion of ethical significance. The sources supply competing philosophical accounts, not empirical verification or a completed derivation.

## Protective-activity review and correction of the burden of argument

Section 8's former next-test wording overemphasized the object protected by an identity restriction. The rival need not assert a right to exist, prefer A or oppose B; it can deny the proposed comparative reason. The revised ending and §9 now distinguish the absence of an objection from a positive protective ground. This is a substantive correction, with the old wording retained in the edit record.

The generic control allows a pairwise account to favor protection for each independently selected future person even when their identity is unknown. Only the second configuration changes who would form. Its identity consequence must follow from an independently defended causal and identity account; timing, model identifiers and the word incidental do not establish it or its irrelevance. The intervention's hazard-reducing effect supplies the candidate point. Matched ineffective or worsening effects test that attribution without proving an A/B order by transitivity or recommending manufactured adversity.

The existing-family undertaking provides a real limiting relation. Its validity and content remain to establish, and an actual protected opportunity can constrain the means or whole action. The protective point does not itself transfer authority. Nonexistence is not a welfare state and no future beneficiary inherits another possible person's counterfactual improvement.

The primary comparison retains a crucial scope difference: Martin's examined comparative objection is not a blanket refutation of Kumar's explicitly noncomparative basis. Neither source establishes all the generative account's actor or patient scope, nor is its entire ethical framework adopted. Generic descriptions must answer to actual possible lives; an abstract type is no new subject.

The two argument reviewers accepted the mechanism contrast as a bounded contested positive judgment, distinct from a deductive transfer of q's reason. Complete-text review is recorded in the [protective-activity edit record](FUTURE-PREVENTION-EDITS.json); [checks](FUTURE-PREVENTION-CHECKS.json) concern owned text, references, source metadata and unchanged inspected Lean files. The full ethical minimum and no-assumptions foundation remain open.

### Protection when its consequences change who will exist

The [worked continuation](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/FUTURE-BEARER-FORMATION-ARGUMENT.md#9-protective-activity-when-formation-changes-identity) compares removing an environmental source of severe adversity with and without a further effect on formative timing. When identity remains independent, protection can help whoever forms through separate same-person comparisons. When the timing effect changes identity, the claim that one particular person benefits must be withdrawn. The intervention can nevertheless retain its positive point: worthwhile life develops without the identified adverse condition. An ineffective change with the same timing effect lacks that protective contribution.

This is the defended prospective ground; it requires no return to its source and does not assign another possible person's benefit to the person who actually forms. Calling the identity consequence incidental does not settle its significance. An independently warranted undertaking protecting an existing family's access can constrain the chosen method, even where no future person has a claim to be created. The [primary comparisons](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/FUTURE-BEARER-FORMATION-SOURCES.md#future-standpoints-kumar-and-martin) preserve generic description, actual claims and unknown versus changed identity. Universal participant scope, duties and a complete ordering remain further claims.
